title: Plymouth Satellite Engines by Year (1965–1974)
description: Every factory engine in the Plymouth Satellite and Sport Satellite by year, 1965–1974: the 273 and 318, the 383, the 426 Street Hemi and the 400.
intro: The Satellite was Plymouth's mid-size car from 1965 to 1974: the top of the Belvedere line until 1970, and from 1971 the name for the whole intermediate range. The Road Runner and GTX were related models and have their own pages.
Pick a year to see every engine offered that model year, with its code, rated horsepower and the trims it came in. Each engine links to its full specs.
The early Satellite was V8-only, from the 273 to the 383, with the 426 Street Wedge in 1965 and the 426 Street Hemi offered from 1966.
The 1968 redesign added the 225 slant six to the Satellite; the 383 was the top engine outside the Road Runner and GTX.
From 1971 the Satellite name covered sedans, wagons and the Sebring coupe. Ratings are SAE net from 1972, and the 400 replaced the 383.

excluded.name: 360 V8
excluded.researchNote: Searched the 1971 Satellite brochure engine chart (lists 225, 318, 383-2, 383-4, 440, 440+6, Hemi only), Wikipedia LA 360 applications, Hagerty, Curbside Classic: no 1971 Satellite 360. Likely an NHRA carry-over from its Fury heading (same code C-360-15). Do not show.

excluded.name: 440 V8
excluded.researchNote: The 1972 Satellite engine chart marks the 440 4-bbl and 440 6-bbl NA on every Satellite except Road Runner (where it made the GTX). Searched Wikipedia, Hagerty, Curbside Classic: no non-Road-Runner 1972 Satellite 440 (police/wagon 440 not checked; the wagon catalog is a separate brochure). Do not show for Satellite/Sebring.

excluded.name: 400 V8

sources.name: Plymouth 1974 Satellite folder (Canada), Engine & Transmission Specifications / Engine Application by Model p.3

excluded.researchNote: SAE net. Searched Hagerty (lists only 318/150 and 400/205 for 1974 Satellite/Sebring), Wikipedia (Satellite infobox omits the 400; B-engine article gives only a generic 260 hp high-performance 4-bbl), Curbside Classic: no third source names the 250 hp 400 in a 1974 non-Road-Runner Satellite. The same engine is confirmed in the 1974 Road Runner.

excluded.name: 360 V8
excluded.researchNote: The 1974 factory folder lists only the 360 2-bbl (180) for non-Road-Runner Satellites and the 360 4-bbl (245) for Road Runner. No other source found for a 200 hp 360 in the Satellite. Do not show.

method: Every engine and year listed here was confirmed by at least three independent sources: the NHRA Stock Car Classification Guides, factory material such as GM Heritage Center information kits and sales brochures, EPA records and established references. Several Wikipedia articles count as one source. Where sources give different ratings, the factory figure is shown and the difference is noted. Factory race-only packages need two sources.
